observations.why: Frames the speaker's own perspective as an owned asset kept by the reader, appealing to self-origination; region-only.
Owned-versus-rented framing treats intelligence as a priced holding and an ownership choice, a proportional cost-and-consequence move rather than a relational one.

evidence.quote: Owned intelligence is not the same as rented intelligence.

positions.name: OwnedVersusRentedIntelligence
positions.frame: Where does the value of an organization's intelligence sit when the underlying substrate can be swapped out: in what the organization owns, or in what it rents?
positions.why: Both statements read the same directional question. src-2 sets owned intelligence against rented intelligence as a contrast. src-3 says the substrate is a commodity and the perspective is the asset the reader keeps, which places the value in the perspective and not the substrate. The memo argues the point rather than settling it, so this is a claim-level group with no tension inside it.

placements.title: From rented substrate to owned perspective
placements.frame: Where does each expression locate the value of an organization's intelligence: in the substrate that can be swapped out, or in the perspective the organization keeps?
placements.why: The position OwnedVersusRentedIntelligence holds src-2 (owned intelligence is not the same as rented intelligence) and src-3 (the substrate is a commodity; the perspective is the asset you keep). Both place the lasting value in what the organization owns, namely its perspective, and not in the rented or swappable substrate. The thematic subject, owned versus rented intelligence, is one future envelopes are likely to keep feeding. No existing leaf is present in the supplied structure, so this is a foundational mint.
